subject: Tactile demo follow-up — parity probes, hallucination baseline, next tests
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@tactile.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Li <anna@tactile.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — quick clarifications

Thanks for the walkthrough today — Anna and I noted a few things we want to validate before a deeper evaluation: 

- Can you reproduce your latency & cost numbers when we route through our VPC (we have strict egress controls)?
- We saw a few examples where the model invented entity attributes (e.g., "Company X acquired Y in 2019" when it did not). Can you share how you measure hallucination rates?
- We want a short probe set (100 prompts) that covers our domain for parity testing against HyperscaleXL and CloudEdge. Do you have a suggested seed set?

If you can share a brief plan and any attachments, we can slot a 30-minute technical sync Thursday.

Samir
Head of Product, Tactile Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@tactile.ai>, Anna Li <anna@tactile.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — quick clarifications

Samir — appreciate the clear asks. Quick replies below and attached a first-pass probe package.

1) VPC routing + latency/cost: Redwood Private can be deployed inside your VPC with egress controls; our benchmarks inside similar VPCs show median token latency increase of ~7–12% vs hosted due to networking, and cost delta depends on instance footprint. We'll run the same prompt set inside your VPC connector and share per-route token breakdowns.

2) Hallucination measurement: we use a two-pronged approach — precision/recall-style factuality checks (ground-truth entity tables) and a conservative hallucination labeler that flags assertions lacking provenance. For the probe package we include a small adjudication rubric and an automated scorer that outputs hallucination_rate and severity buckets.

3) Probe set: attached "probe-prompt-set-v1.txt" (100 prompts) tuned to your domain plus a CSV of results from the quick run against our hosted Redwood-3.2 baseline. Recommended next tests: parity vs HyperscaleXL and CloudEdge (same prompts, same temperature/decoding), hallucination adjudication, and regression runs on your historic prompts.

Proposed next steps (action items):
- Redwood: run the 100-probe set inside Tactile VPC connector (ETA 48–72h) — Rishi
- Tactile: share a short list of protected entities / gold-table for adjudication (ETA Tue EOD) — Samir
- Joint: 30-min tech sync Thurs 10:00am PT to review initial deltas and agree on extended probe plan — Anna + Rishi + Marissa

Attachments: tactile-probe-summary.csv, probe-prompt-set-v1.txt, redwood-differentiators-one-pager.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

— Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Anna Li <anna@tactile.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@tactile.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — quick clarifications

Rishi — thanks, that plan looks good. A couple clarifications before the sync: 

- For the hallucination adjudication, can your scorer export the specific token spans you flagged? That helps our annotators triage quickly.
- On the VPC run: we will provide a temporary egress rule for a testing subnet — security wants to know the exact IP/port ranges Redwood will use.

We'll bring the gold-table by Tuesday EOD and confirm the Thur 10am slot.

Anna
ML Lead, Tactile Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@tactile.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Anna Li <anna@tactile.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — prioritization and quick wins

Looping back after the quick runs — Monica and I reviewed the 100-probe results attached and prioritized a short validation matrix: 

Priority 1 (run this in the Tactile VPC first):
- Latency delta by prompt length bucket (<=64, 65–256, >256 tokens) — essential for your interactive product UX.
- Hallucination severity high (assertions about financials/mergers) — we saw 6 high-severity cases in the baseline.

Priority 2 (parallel runs):
- Parity runs vs HyperscaleXL and CloudEdge using identical decoding seeds (we can coordinate with them if you want).
- Regression sweep on your historical support prompts to see if behavior changes under load.

Deliverables & owners: 
- Redwood: VPC probe run + per-prompt latency + token-cost breakdown (ETA Tue 48–72h) — Monica
- Redwood: Hallucination span export + adjudication CSV with suggested severity tags (ETA Tue) — Marissa
- Tactile: Gold-table + protected entities CSV (ETA Tue EOD) — Samir
- Joint: Follow-up sync Tue (optional) / Thu 10am PT (confirmed) to triage high-severity hallucinations — All

A couple of notes on competitive framing (short):
- Hyperscalers often prioritize throughput at the expense of tight latency SLOs for interactive traffic; Redwood's continuous batching and KV cache controls let you tune for lower tail latency on mid-size prompts.
- For hallucination mitigation, our adjudication pipeline connects outputs to provenance (when available) and supports deterministic reranking against a retrieval pass.

I'll join Thu's sync and bring sample adjudication outputs so we can quickly triage the 6 high-severity issues. 

— Marissa
Head of Inference Evals, Redwood Inference
